title: LONGEVITY SURVIVOR v2.2 — Resolution Gate Kinetic Killer Test
frozen_claim: Across mammalian regenerative systems, successful regeneration should show a shorter-lived controlled wound-state followed by timely EXIT, whereas scarring should reflect persistence of the same wound-state.

measurement_rule.priority: measure appearance -> peak -> decay/clearance of cellular wound states rather than pathway abundance alone
measurement_rule.true_half_life: Only report a half-life when quantitative time-series permit a defensible decay estimate.
measurement_rule.interval_censored_lifetime: If publications provide only discrete sampling points, report the interval in which disappearance/resolution occurs; do not invent an exponential t1/2.
measurement_rule.state_identity_rule: Marker disappearance is not equivalent to lineage disappearance; follow fate transitions when lineage tracing or state-resolved data exist.
measurement_rule.spatial_rule: The same marker in distinct anatomical compartments must not be merged into one state.

kinetics.1_2_dpi: clear lesion gap; microglia accumulate and activate
kinetics.3_dpi: fibronectin+ bridge present; activated CD68+/SPP1+ microglia occupy lesion; Fn1-expressing repair state detected
kinetics.5_dpi: Fn1 lesion expression no longer detected in the reported in situ time series
kinetics.7_dpi: fibronectin signal disappeared; gap refilled; most microglia ramified, P2Y12+, SPP1-/CD68-
kinetics.14_dpi: blood-derived CCR2+ macrophages absent and lesion remains largely scar-free

tissues.kinetic_bound: Fn1-high lesion state detectable at 3 dpi and absent at 5 dpi; bridge present at 3 dpi and gone by 7 dpi; activated microglia return to homeostatic phenotype within ~1 week.
tissues.nonregenerative_control: Adult spinal-cord lesions retain CD68+ activated microglia/macrophages and monocyte-derived macrophages through at least 14 dpi and form mature scar architecture.
tissues.causal_support: Microglia depletion impairs neonatal bridge formation and axon regrowth; neonatal microglia or peptidase-inhibitor-treated adult microglia improve adult lesion healing.

tissues.state: transient alpha-SMA+ extrinsic helper cells plus transient fibrotic-marker program

kinetics.3_dpi: abundant alpha-SMA+ ScxGFP-negative cells occupy gap; intrinsic Scx+ tenocytes proliferate near cut ends
kinetics.7_dpi: scar-associated transcripts including alpha-SMA begin transient upregulation
kinetics.14_dpi: only limited alpha-SMA immunostaining remains in neonatal neo-tendon while adult scar shows intense alpha-SMA/laminin
kinetics.28_dpi: neonatal scar-associated transcripts return to control range; tendon-lineage program remains elevated

tissues.kinetic_bound: Helper-cell alpha-SMA abundance is high at day 3 and markedly reduced by day 14; fibrotic transcript program resolves by day 28. Sampling is insufficient for a true t1/2.
tissues.nonregenerative_control: Adult tendon shows persistent fibrotic repair; independent adult flexor-tendon lineage studies detect alpha-SMA+ myofibroblasts through days 28-35 with disappearance by ~day 42, depending on model and compartment.
tissues.causal_support: TGF-beta signaling is required for neonatal tenocyte recruitment and functional regeneration; macrophage depletion impairs neonatal regeneration, but a direct EXIT-specific perturbation of neonatal alpha-SMA helper clearance remains missing.

tissues.model: adult Acomys cahirinus regenerative ear-pinna injury versus Mus scarring control

kinetics.weeks_1_2: myofibroblasts appear rapidly in both Acomys and Mus
kinetics.weeks_3_4: Acomys ear myofibroblasts resolve as wound closure/blastema differentiation progress; Mus myofibroblasts persist
kinetics.causal_perturbation: YAP-TEAD inhibition prolongs Acomys myofibroblast persistence and converts regenerative healing toward fibrosis

tissues.kinetic_bound: Acomys ear myofibroblast state is transient on the scale of ~1-3 weeks; exact t1/2 requires source-data reconstruction.
tissues.causal_support: Direct in vivo perturbation links delayed myofibroblast resolution to loss of regenerative outcome.

tissues.model: adult Acomys full-thickness dorsal skin wound versus Mus; sampled d0,7,14,21,28,35,70

kinetics.day_7: ~75% of upper wound-bed cells are alpha-SMA+ in both Mus and Acomys
kinetics.day_14: Acomys upper dermal wound-bed alpha-SMA effectively disappears while Mus remains strongly positive; Acomys simultaneously develops a strong lower alpha-SMA+ bridge between panniculus carnosus ends
kinetics.day_21_plus: Acomys dermal myofibroblasts remain cleared while panniculus-associated alpha-SMA bridge remains intense for weeks during muscle regeneration

tissues.killer_observation: A long-lived alpha-SMA+ wound-associated state can coexist with successful regeneration when it is spatially routed into a regenerative scaffold compartment.

tissues.state: dermal alpha-SMA+ myofibroblasts / wound fibroblast states

kinetics.~day_7: myofibroblasts become prominent; fibroblast wound-state transcriptomic cluster peaks around day 7 in multiple datasets
kinetics.weeks_2_3: classical reviews report greatest myofibroblast content during second and third weeks
kinetics.later: myofibroblast abundance declines, while collagenous scar and remodeled ECM persist

tissues.killer_observation: Persistent scar does not require indefinite persistence of alpha-SMA+ myofibroblasts.

tissues.model: neonatal mouse apex resection / neonatal MI literature

kinetics.48_hours: fibronectin/tenascin-C deposition, immune infiltrate and alpha-SMA+ myofibroblasts appear after neonatal apex resection
kinetics.7_days: inflammation largely resolves while myofibroblasts are more frequent
kinetics.21_days: alpha-SMA restricted mainly to vessels in one apex-resection series; in neonatal MI studies fibrosis can be present through days 1-17 and nearly disappear by day 21

tissues.kinetic_bound: Regenerative neonatal cardiac wound programs can occupy a multi-day to ~3-week window and then resolve/reorganize; exact behavior depends strongly on injury model and resection size.

kinetics.day_3_4: alpha-SMA+ myofibroblasts appear; proliferation peaks around early proliferative phase
kinetics.day_7: alpha-SMA remains high while ECM production is robust
kinetics.day_10: alpha-SMA becomes only partially detectable / lineage studies show myofibroblast marker loss
kinetics.day_14: alpha-SMA myofibroblast phenotype largely absent, but scar maturation continues
kinetics.day_28: periostin-positive / activated or scar-maintaining fibroblast populations and ECM maintenance can persist

tissues.killer_observation: Scar can persist after the alpha-SMA myofibroblast state has exited because fibroblasts transition into alternate scar-maintaining states and ECM becomes stabilized/crosslinked.

killed.reason: Acomys panniculus-associated alpha-SMA+ bridge persists for weeks while tissue regenerates.
Adult cardiac myofibroblasts lose alpha-SMA by ~10-14 days while scar persists via state transition and ECM maturation; adult skin scars also persist after myofibroblast decline.
Marker duration is compartment- and fate-dependent and can be regenerative, fibrotic or merely transitional.

survives.name: WOUND_STATE_FATE_ROUTING_AND_RESOLUTION_GATE
survives.formula: ENTRY -> TEMPORARY_OR_SUPPORTIVE_WOUND_STATE -> SPATIAL_ROUTING -> HANDOFF_TO_REBUILD -> PROFIBROTIC_OUTPUT_TERMINATION -> FATE_SWITCH_OR_CLEARANCE -> HOMEOSTASIS
survives.key_variable: Not raw persistence time, but whether wound-state occupancy remains in a pro-fibrotic attractor versus being cleared, re-differentiated, spatially redirected or converted into a regenerative-support state.

strongest_positive_support: Neonatal spinal cord: rapid microglial Fn1 bridge state and return to homeostasis, with causal depletion/transplantation evidence.
Acomys ear skin: myofibroblast resolution correlates with regeneration and experimentally delaying resolution causes fibrosis.
Neonatal tendon: transient alpha-SMA helper/fibrotic program followed by intrinsic tenocyte recruitment and neo-tendon formation.
strongest_negative_controls: Adult heart: alpha-SMA state ends yet scar persists via alternate fibroblast state + ECM stabilization.
Acomys full-thickness skin: a long-lived alpha-SMA bridge can be pro-regenerative when spatially assigned to muscle reconstruction.
cross_tissue_result.interpretation: The common mammalian control candidate is not a universal half-life threshold. It is a state-routing/termination architecture that decides whether a wound program hands off into regeneration, redirects into a useful temporary scaffold, or locks into scar-maintaining ECM/cell states.

next_killer_tests.test: Reconstruct quantitative state-occupancy curves from source data for neonatal spinal microglia, Acomys ear myofibroblasts, neonatal tendon alpha-SMA cells, adult cardiac fibroblast states and Acomys full-thickness dermal versus panniculus compartments.
next_killer_tests.output: normalized fraction-of-state versus tau, with interval-censored clearance and state-transition edges

next_killer_tests.test: Track lineage fate after marker loss: apoptosis, de-differentiation, re-differentiation, spatial relocation, or transition into scar-maintaining matrifibrocyte-like state.
next_killer_tests.reason: Marker disappearance alone cannot define EXIT.

next_killer_tests.test: Compare persistence of profibrotic OUTPUT rather than alpha-SMA marker: collagen I/III deposition, periostin, crosslinking, matrix alignment, stiffness, and MMP/TIMP balance.
next_killer_tests.reason: Scar memory can persist in ECM after cellular activation changes.

next_killer_tests.test: Mechanical-lock third-tissue causal test remains open: seek a developmental/regenerative model where experimentally changing native ECM mechanics shifts regeneration-versus-scar outcome without relying only on an implanted biomaterial context.

shareability.safe_claim: A cross-tissue comparison suggests that mammalian regenerative outcome is better predicted by wound-state fate, spatial routing and termination of profibrotic output than by the half-life of a single activated-cell marker. Existing data provide causal examples and counterexamples that falsify a simple short-state-versus-persistent-state model.
not_yet_allowed: claim of a universal mammalian resolution gate
claim of a new therapeutic target
claim of human rejuvenation or clinical applicability
